newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's UNITA says it has 3,000 Zairean refugees.
newsitem.headline: Angola's UNITA says it has 3,000 Zairean refugees.

text.p: Angola's former rebel UNITA movement said on Tuesday about 3,000 former Zairean refugees were camping in an area controlled by the movement in the northeast of the country.
"These people are from Zaire and some are Hutus from Rwanda," UNITA"s General Horacio Junjuvili told Reuters.
"Most of them are women and children and we are doing our best to take care of them," he added.
Junjuvili said aid organisations were free to travel to the refugee camp at the town of Lovua near Angola's eastern border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly Zaire.
But aid officials say they are awaiting formal approval from the Angolan government to travel to the area.

The refugees fled a seven-month-long military conflict between the forces of ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko and Laurent Kabila, who is now president. Kabila renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo last month.
